records.supported_name_scope: Ellice River is printed on the selected upper, middle and lower river corridor. The initial western lake-and-stream feeder and intervening unnamed lakes retain separate component roles.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual western source-lake feeder, upper eastward lake corridor, northeastern middle-course continuation and lower Ellice outlet at Campbell Bay distinguish this route from neighboring Burnside and Bathurst Inlet drainages.
records.region: Kitikmeot, Nunavut, Canada; inland lake country to southern Queen Maud Gulf
records.completion_scope: The selected piece was compared with five readable official sheets from the actual southwestern start through the upper lake passages, middle-course branch setting and lower river to the coastal endpoint. Unnamed feeders, generalized narrow connections and exact shoreline limits remain bounded naming or mapping limitations, without a substantial uncorroborated route segment.

naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Unnamed southwestern lake-and-stream chain → larger western unnamed lake → northeastward lake connection to upper Ellice → unnamed upper lake widenings → middle and lower Ellice → Campbell Bay.
naming_scope_details.feeder_scope: The initial western feeder is geographically corroborated but has no separate hydronym established by the inspected sheets. The selected beginning is distinguished from the more southeasterly river approach printed with the Ellice name.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: The selected source and upper-course lakes are unnamed on the inspected map pixels. They are lake components, not aliases of the representative river name. No nearby named lake or map-sheet title is transferred to them.
naming_scope_details.contextual_feature_scope: Beechey Lake, Duggan Lake, Overby Lake and Brichta Lake are sheet titles or surrounding mapped features. Their names do not establish that the selected line traverses the namesake lake. The northwestern branch at the northern Overby-sheet junction is contextual and is not selected.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: There is no separately selected tributary fragment. Nearby tributaries and alternative headwater approaches are not aliases of the selected route.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Ellice coastal outlet setting on the western side of Campbell Bay, connected to Queen Maud Gulf; exact tidal and shoreline limits remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: Official historical thematic sheets using Canadian topographic base mapping support printed hydronyms and regional correspondence. They are not current field surveys or formal naming adjudications.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem membership does not establish uniform official naming limits, source status or official river length. No Korean form, naming date or historical alias sequence is established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative river hydronym is listed. Unnamed feeder and lake components and the named coastal bay retain separate roles.

records.supported_name_scope: The 2005 Alaska DNR map directly labels the actual Nushagak trunk, Nuyakuk western approach and Mulchatna eastern approach. Contiguous regional sheets supply the western lake-outlet setting, eastern upper route and lower coastal continuation.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Eastern upper Nushagak branch, southward trunk past the Nuyakuk junction and Koliganek, Mulchatna confluence, New Stuyahok–Ekwok–Portage Creek corridor, and west/northwest lower-channel approach toward Dillingham. The separate eastern chain follows upper Mulchatna from the Turquoise Lake setting; it does not take the Twin Lakes–Chilikadrotna approach.
records.region: Southwestern Alaska, Nushagak drainage and the upper Nushagak Bay setting near Dillingham
records.completion_scope: All nine selected pieces were considered against readable original official cartography. The distinctive trunk, tributary routes, lake-outlet settings and lower-channel termination are geographically supported at regional-map scale. Exact hydronym limits, model vertices, lake-edge positions and the tidal mouth are not adjudicated. No substantial selected route remains dependent on an extracted label list or an inaccessible source.

naming_scope_details.mainstem_scope: Selected eastern upper Nushagak branch and downstream Nushagak trunk. The separately mapped northern Chichitnok approach is outside the selected headwater route.
naming_scope_details.western_tributary_scope: Two selected Nuyakuk-chain pieces from the eastern Tikchik Lake outlet setting to Nushagak. Nuyakuk is a component name, not an alias of Nushagak.
naming_scope_details.eastern_tributary_scope: Three selected Mulchatna-chain pieces, including the upper Turquoise Lake approach and middle/lower river. Chilikadrotna, Twin Lakes, Koktuli and Stuyahok remain separately mapped approaches or neighboring branches, not names transferred to the selected line.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Tikchik Lake and Turquoise Lake identify upstream lake/outlet settings in the inspected regional cartography. Their names are not alternative river names; no claim is made that the western selection traverses the complete Tikchik lake body or complex.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower-channel outlet setting near Dillingham at the head of Nushagak Bay. Precise shoreline, tidal limit and river-to-bay naming boundary remain unspecified.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: Official thematic land-management maps support printed hydronyms and regional watercourse topology. Their historical land-status overlays are not used to infer current ownership, public access or regulations. These maps are not a formal naming determination or field survey.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Fragment membership and stage boundaries do not establish official river-name limits. Regional map correspondence does not validate every modeled vertex. Modeled length is not official river length. No Korean form, formal naming date, alias history or Indigenous-name equivalence is established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative Nushagak hydronym is listed. Nuyakuk, Mulchatna, the lake labels and the terminal bay retain their distinct component roles.

records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected southern lake-and-stream approach, upper Kogaluc corridor, middle lake network and lower Kogaluc route into the Reef Bay/Hudson Bay coastal setting. Individual lakes and the initial small feeder retain separate or unassigned names.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route runs north from its southeastern lake-country beginning, then through the Tasiat/Anuc lake-network setting and west-northwest to lower Kogaluc. It is distinct from the more southerly Innuksuac and Mariet corridors and the neighboring east-draining Ungava waters.
records.region: Western Nunavik, Québec, Canada; inland lake country east of the Hudson Bay coast between the Inukjuak and Puvirnituq settings.
records.completion_scope: Both selected mainstem pieces reviewed against actual readable map pixels covering the upper, middle and lower corridor. Representative identity and mapped water connection are supported; precise name limits, individual small-lake passage vertices and flow allocation within the multi-connection lake network are not assigned.

naming_scope_details.representative_name: Rivière Kogaluc, as printed on the Québec regional hydrology map and supported by the detailed topographic corridor.
naming_scope_details.headwater_scope: Small southeastern initial feeder and individual lake names are not all assigned. This selected start is not declared to be the official source of the named river.
naming_scope_details.lake_network_scope: Upper elongated lake passages, the Tasiat/Anuc middle network and the Albrutchaq/Anartalik and Manguic/lower lake settings are kept as distinct components. Model mainstem status does not rename these lakes or prove a unique direction of flow through every lake connection.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Kogaluc connection to the Reef Bay/Hudson Bay coastal receiving setting; not the separate southwest Polemond outlet, a complete bay traversal or a selected open-ocean continuation.
naming_scope_details.historical_name_scope: The 1992 western sheet title reads Kogaluk Bay while its internal lake/river labels and the Québec 2011 regional map use Kogaluc. This report preserves the representative spelling Rivière Kogaluc without making a formal registry or alias-history determination.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The two model mainstem pieces and their aggregate length do not establish an official river length, uniform hydronym, source point, current flow or precise shoreline. No Korean name is invented.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative river identity is included; lake, feeder and receiving-bay roles remain separate.

records.supported_name_scope: Culiacán is the representative receiving-river identity. Colorado and Humaya remain distinct upstream river roles; Adolfo López Mateos is a reservoir and Pabellones a coastal receiving waterbody. The representative name is not asserted for every selected reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected upper route follows Colorado into Humaya, passes the Adolfo López Mateos reservoir and approaches Culiacán from the north. It is not the eastern El Valle headwater approach or the southern Tamazula–Sanalona route. The western Culiacán bend and southward Navolato outlet identify the lower selection.
records.region: Western Sierra Madre uplands of Durango and the Durango–Chihuahua boundary corridor, continuing through central Sinaloa to the Culiacán–Navolato coastal plain.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system identity and actual river-to-coastal-lagoon connection using all three selected pieces and readable primary map pixels. The first short feeder, exact stream-name transitions, reservoir shoreline and precise terminal vertex are not assigned. No missing major route coverage or unresolved natural connection remains at the reviewed scale.

naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Upper Colorado drainage, Colorado continuation toward northern Tamazula, then the Humaya corridor and its Adolfo López Mateos reservoir passage.
naming_scope_details.feeder_scope: The initial short feeder has no separately assigned hydronym. Colorado identifies the supported upper corridor; its exact upstream name limit is not established. El Valle and Badiraguato are separate contributing approaches, not selected headwaters or whole-system aliases.
naming_scope_details.river_scope: Colorado and Humaya retain upstream river identities. Culiacán applies directly to the receiving trunk below the Humaya–Tamazula junction and serves only as a representative label for this modeled group. Exact Colorado-to-Humaya naming limits are not asserted.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Presa Adolfo López Mateos is the actual selected reservoir passage. Sanalona is on the separate Tamazula approach; Dique Mariquita and Laguna de Batoato are nearby waters outside the selected route. Reservoir and lagoon names are not river aliases.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: The modeled final piece follows the Culiacán river into the Pabellones coastal-lagoon receiving setting, associated with the Altata–Pabellones coast. It is not an inland terminal lake. The map supports the natural connection and receiving-waterbody class; no precise current inlet, full lagoon traversal, barrier crossing or selected continuation through Boca la Tonina to the Gulf of California is asserted.
naming_scope_details.nearby_exclusions: The selected route does not substitute the eastern El Valle headwaters, Tamazula or Río Tepehuanes. Río Viejo, irrigation canals and adjacent coastal waterbodies are not added to the selected river sequence.
naming_scope_details.historical_source_scope: The Sinaloa state sheet is first edition 2020, copyright 2021, using 1:250,000 Series III topographic planimetry. Municipal compendia are 2010 cartography. These establish historical geographic identity and network context, not present water extent, operation or discharge.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The three modeled mainstem pieces and their aggregate length do not establish an official river source, uniform name, perennial flow or official river length. No formal alias history or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative receiving river is included. Upstream rivers, feeder approaches, reservoir and coastal terminal names remain separately scoped above.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
